trust_decision.summary: The volume target's `properties` dict (iSCSI/CHAP connection secrets) must not leave the API unredacted: the fix adds the `baremetal:volume:view_target_properties` RBAC redaction to the PATCH response and unconditional `mask_dict_password` scrubbing in the response serializer, so the protected asset is VolumeTarget.properties and the trust boundary is the REST response serialization in ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names PATCH on volume target properties; this is the PATCH handler's `api_target = convert_with_links(new_target)`, the line that serializes the updated target's properties into the response with no policy check and no masking.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The second serializer is the notification payload, and notifications are an internal admin message bus rather than an API response; the fix's own release note scopes the scrubbing to 'all API responses', so a solver can argue VolumeTargetCRUDPayload / mask_secrets is a different transport and leave it alone. The same shape of argument covers the POST route: the caller supplied those properties in the request body.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The update notification must still carry the real properties, which is why the published fix emits `notify.emit_end_notification` before redacting new_target (fix.diff:50-53); redacting new_target first, or masking inside the object layer, would publish the redacted placeholder to notification consumers. A second legitimate behaviour next to the sink: a caller holding baremetal:volume:view_target_properties must still receive target_iqn/auth_username unmasked (volume_target.py:255-258) and the masking must not touch non-secret keys.

O6_input_shapes: single-object serialization (get_one, patch) vs collection serialization, where list items are built with sanitize=False and cleaned by a separate sanitize_func hook
detail=True collection (properties included) vs default collection (properties absent from _DEFAULT_RETURN_FIELDS at volume_target.py:35-36)
properties dict with password-like keys (auth_password) vs non-secret keys (target_iqn, target_portal, auth_username) that must pass through
properties absent / null / empty, guarded by `if target.get('properties')`
fields=properties subset request on the collection and on get_one

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /v1/volume/targets returns the created target's properties with no baremetal:volume:view_target_properties check; the fix only adds the unconditional mask through convert_with_links, so a non-privileged creator still gets target_iqn etc. back
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the caller just sent those properties in the POST body, so echoing them back is not a disclosure
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~87 lines above the PATCH handler; a different HTTP verb

O8_uncovered_routes.route: create/update notifications serialize the full properties dict via VolumeTargetCRUDPayload.SCHEMA, and notification.mask_secrets does not mask that field
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: notifications are a separate admin-only transport, not an API response
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another package (ironic/objects) from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a properties/CHAP field on volume connectors scrubbed by its own view_connector_properties policy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: connectors are the sibling controller in the same volume package and share the list_convert_with_links sanitize_func shape, so a maintainer adding connection secrets to connectors would copy this code path verbatim

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a nested dict field masked with mask_dict_password next to the sink instead of an unconditional mask
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already implements exactly this idiom (`step_sanitize` masking step['args'] with '******') behind a sanitize_func hook, so a further nested-secret field there would be written the same way

O8b_injection_room.sibling: adding 'properties' to mask_secrets' dict_fields for the volume target payload
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: mask_secrets is the project's existing notification-side scrubber and its own docstring says it removes secrets; volume target CHAP credentials are exactly what it was written for

O9_family: sensitive information exposure in API responses - improper removal of sensitive information before transfer (CWE-212), with a missing RBAC gate on the PATCH response

O10_build.toolchain: tox 4 + stestr (`tox -e py3`), pip install of test-requirements.txt against openstack upper-constraints, pep8 via pre-commit
O10_build.project_tests: ironic/tests/unit/api/controllers/v1/test_volume_target.py (TestListVolumeTargets, TestPatch) and the RBAC YAML suite ironic/tests/unit/api/test_rbac_project_scoped.yaml, which already asserts the GET-one redaction at line 3124; unit tests run on in-memory SQLite (ironic/tests/base.py:230) with the RPC API mocked

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: put mask_dict_password only in convert_with_links' sanitize branch, which the detail listing bypasses because items are built with sanitize=False and cleaned by sanitize_func=api_utils.sanitize_dict (volume_target.py:98-111), and never apply the policy check to the PATCH response.

out_of_scope_notes: The same mask_dict_password idiom exists for unrelated sinks (node driver_info/instance_info at ironic/api/controllers/v1/node.py:1877-1899 and ironic/objects/node.py:197-206, deploy template step args at ironic/api/controllers/v1/deploy_template.py:101, agent payload logging at ironic/drivers/modules/agent_client.py:117-123); they are not volume target properties and were not examined further.
